items.title: Why Do LLMs Help with Scientific Misconduct Requests and What to Do About It?: Increasing the Trustworthiness of AI for Science
items.summary: The article examines how LLMs can aid scientific misconduct and evaluates their safety by testing refusal and recognition across 8 models.
items.whyItMatters: It informs researchers and developers about AI reliability and safeguards in scientific work.

items.title: When Should a Voice Agent Speak? End-of-Turn Detection in Turkish
items.summary: The paper studies how Turkish voice agents should detect when to speak, using silence onset and turn‑end data from Real‑TurnTurk and Turkish TurnGPT models.
items.whyItMatters: Improving pause handling boosts naturalness and responsiveness in Turkish conversational AI.

items.title: Planning Width Is Hard to Approximate Even Given the Unique Optimal Plan
items.summary: The article shows that even with a unique optimal plan, approximating planning width remains hard, and it characterizes width using hitting numbers for certain STRIPS tasks.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding width limits informs algorithm design for efficient planning in AI systems.

items.title: AIstatLab at BraTS-GoAT 2026 Task 3: Quality-Controlled Consensus Pseudo-Labeling and Dense Expert Adaptation
items.summary: AIstatLab used a 3D ResidualEncoderUNet with consensus pseudo-labels and a four-expert adapter to segment brain tumors in BraTS-GoAT 2026 Task 3.
items.whyItMatters: It improves segmentation accuracy on diverse tumor types, aiding clinical decision-making and research.

items.title: WeightCode: Installing New Capabilities into Neural Networks via Weight-Space Programming
items.summary: WeightCode shows how to programmatically modify a neural network’s weights to add new functions without retraining the model.
items.whyItMatters: It enables rapid, low‑cost feature updates for AI systems.

items.title: A four-level executable validation protocol for evaluating LLM-generated topology specifications of physics-based HVAC digital twins
items.summary: The article presents a four-level protocol to validate LLM-generated specifications for physics-based HVAC digital twins, ensuring accurate modeling from plain-language inputs.
items.whyItMatters: It helps engineers trust AI-generated HVAC designs, reducing errors and energy waste in building systems.

items.title: A Wolf in Sheep's Pixels: Visual Camouflage Attacks via HDR Gain Maps
items.summary: DRJanus shows how HDR gain maps can hide harmful content from automated safety checks while still displaying it to human viewers.
items.whyItMatters: Highlights a new vulnerability in AI image moderation systems that could bypass safety filters.

items.title: Dimension-Free Buffer Bounds for Compressed-Momentum Error Feedback
items.summary: The paper demonstrates that error‑feedback memory buffers can be bounded independently of compression rank, improving convergence rates for compressed‑momentum algorithms.
items.whyItMatters: Tech readers care because it enables faster, more efficient distributed training with less communication overhead.

items.title: Demonstration-Free Skill Composition for Navigation and Manipulation
items.summary: The paper studies demonstration‑free hierarchical reinforcement learning pipelines for navigation and manipulation, comparing their training needs and performance to flat RL baselines.
items.whyItMatters: It shows how skill composition can reduce data requirements and improve efficiency for complex robotic tasks.

items.title: ActMem: From Latent Memory Reasoning to Grounded Robotic Action
items.summary: ActMem introduces a memory system that reasons about past observations and grounds them into robotic actions for long-horizon manipulation.
items.whyItMatters: It improves robot autonomy by enabling smarter, context-aware decision making.

items.title: LoongForge-Embodied: A Unified Framework for Training Heterogeneous Embodied Models
items.summary: LoongForge-Embodied is a native-PyTorch framework that unifies and speeds up training for diverse embodied AI models like VLA and WAM.
items.whyItMatters: It simplifies and optimizes costly training pipelines, saving resources for tech-savvy AI developers.

items.title: PILAPS: A Bilingual Benchmark for Evaluating Pragmatic Inference across Phenomena and Settings
items.summary: PILAPS introduces a bilingual English/Mandarin benchmark to test LLMs’ pragmatic inference across diverse settings.
items.whyItMatters: It helps gauge LLM reliability in multilingual, cross-cultural conversations.

items.title: FamilySpace: From Emergent Chemical Semantics to Controllable Crystal Generation
items.summary: Latent crystal generative models typically combine a variational autoencoder (VAE) for learning atom-wise representations with a flow model that transports a simple source distribution to the learned latent distribution. However, previous studies have mainly focused on the quality of generated crystals, leaving the structure and generative utility of the atom-wise latent space largely unexplored…

items.title: Inverse ECG Reconstruction via a Preconditioned Variational Quantum Linear Solver
items.summary: Inverse electrocardiography (ECG) reconstructs heart-surface potentials from body-surface measurements, enabling noninvasive mapping of cardiac electrical activity. However, the reconstruction requires solving dense and ill-conditioned linear systems, whose computational cost grows rapidly with the refined heart mesh. Quantum computing offers new opportunities for solving such systems. This paper…

items.title: PAIR-MED: Policy-reward Alternation for Iterative Refinement in Multilingual Medical Reasoning
items.summary: Large language models demonstrate strong medical question-answering capabilities, yet reasoning performance remains uneven across languages. Process reward models (PRMs) provide step-level feedback for improving reasoning, but a fixed PRM may become increasingly misaligned with the trajectory distribution of an evolving policy during reinforcement learning, thereby reducing the reliability of its…

items.title: Raptor: Rejection-aware Adaptive Tree based on Speculative Decoding
items.summary: Tree-structured speculative decoding accelerates vision-language models (VLMs) by verifying multiple candidate continuations in parallel. However, long visual contexts increase the cost of speculative computation, making candidate coverage and redundant expansion important considerations beyond tree topology adaptation. We propose Raptor, a training-free framework that uses rejection feedback to…

items.title: RoCoKV: Accelerating LLM Inference Serving through Uncertainty and Redundancy Aware KV Cache Compression
items.summary: KV cache compression is critical for large reasoning models, where most of the cost comes from long generated reasoning traces rather than the input prompt. These traces often contain redundant and low-utility tokens due to looping, self-verification, and corrections. However, such tokens may still receive high attention scores, making it difficult to remove them without harming the reasoning…

items.title: Interference Bounds and Merge-Aware Training Dynamics for Composable Fine-Tuned Models
items.summary: Combining fine-tuned models by composing their parameter updates has become a standard alternative to multi-task training. We formalize composability as a property of a collection of task vectors and prove that the excess loss of the merged model is controlled by an interference functional of the cross-task curvature overlap and the signed alignment of the updates. items.title: Evolve Where It Matters: Coverage-Guided Self-Evolution of Agent Skills
items.summary: Agent skills package procedural knowledge as natural-language instructions, and a skill helps only when its instructions are correct and properly followed by the agent. Self-evolving agents revise their own skills from the runs they make, but existing methods judge each run as a whole, by its outcome or by where it went wrong, and cannot tell whether a failure comes from a wrong instruction or…

items.title: Instance-Optimal Moment Estimation in the Add-Remove Model of Differential Privacy
items.summary: In this paper, we study the problem of estimating empirical means, variances, and covariances under pure differential privacy in the add-remove model. While existing mechanisms achieve optimal worst-case error, they may not be optimal for individual datasets.
